translations.about_text: We are a small community of honey badger fans from Russia, England and Germany, collecting facts and photos about our favourite animal.
translations.hero_subtitle: The most fearless creature on Earth - a fan site.

facts.title: The most fearless animal alive
facts.body: The honey badger is listed in the Guinness Book of Records as the world's most fearless animal. It stands its ground against lions, leopards and hyenas many times its size.

facts.title: Skin like armour
facts.body: Its hide is thick, rubbery and loose enough for a honey badger grabbed by the neck to twist around and bite back. Bee stings, porcupine quills and most snake fangs rarely get through it.

facts.title: A born escape artist
facts.body: Honey badgers are clever problem-solvers. They use tools, stack objects to climb and work out how to open latches, gates and enclosure doors.

facts.title: Shrugs off snake venom
facts.body: Honey badgers hunt and eat cobras and puff adders. A venomous bite can knock one out for hours, but it later wakes up, shakes itself off and finishes the meal.

facts.title: Sweet tooth, steel nerves
facts.body: Honey badgers tear open wild hives for honey and nutritious grubs, paying little attention to the swarm of angry bees.

facts.title: Teamed up with a bird
facts.body: The greater honeyguide leads honey badgers to wild bee nests. The badger breaks the nest open and shares the spoils with the bird, an unusual partnership between a bird and a mammal.

facts.title: Built to dig
facts.body: With its long, powerful front claws, a honey badger can dig a burrow in hard ground within minutes, whether it is hunting, escaping danger or making a den.

facts.title: The legend of Stoffel
facts.body: Stoffel, a honey badger at a South African wildlife centre, became famous for escaping from every enclosure. He scaled walls, opened gates and even stacked rocks and mud to climb over the fence.

facts.title: Found on two continents
facts.body: Honey badgers live across much of sub-Saharan Africa and Asia, from the Arabian Peninsula to India. They are equally at home in deserts and forests.

facts.title: Always on the move
facts.body: A honey badger usually travels alone. It can cover several kilometres a day in search of food, exploring burrows, crevices and anything else that catches its interest.
